data.title: bn-3le: Replace procedural frog with authored mutation atlas

data.body: [P1] Reauthor the production poses against the semantic-ink and pixel-cluster contract. All ten full frames use 8 nontransparent indices although ART-BIBLE.md caps a normal actor at 4-7. Idle uses 9,13,28,51 while omitting 8,31,38 from the declared default frog ramp; run A and B replace three of their eight colors between adjacent frames, so material/color identity flickers with the animation. An 8-neighbor same-role scan also finds 52 isolated colored pixels in idle, 33/47 in run A/B, and 16-44 in every other full pose, versus the contract maximum of two deliberate isolated accents. Rework the atlas with a stable frog-body ramp, <=7 colors per normal frame, connected intentional clusters, and source-palette 1x/flip inspection.

[P2] Add regressions for the actual atlas and palette-scope acceptance unit. These assertions only prove that the whole gameplay framebuffer contains broad scene colors; terrain/background can supply them, so the test passes the currently noncompliant frog and cannot detect a wrong per-frame palette, corrupted allocation, preview-palette leakage, incomplete 1..63 hurt remap, or failure to restore INK_MAP before legacy primitives. Validate each allocated 24x24/8x8 region and its allowed semantic indices, then exercise normal, invulnerable, laser/fire, title, and victory draws with a sentinel legacy primitive after the frog. The builder round-trip is byte-exact in a scratch copy, so that invariant is also cheap to codify.

data.reason: The authored atlas violates the governing semantic-palette and cluster grammar, and the added test does not exercise the atlas or identity/legacy palette boundary.

data.body: Fixed in 5ba9de6: all ten poses now use only the stable hero ramp (5-6 colors), run A/B have identical palettes, and every pose has <=2 isolated same-role accents. Source-palette atlas and live captures regenerated.
